SERVICE OF NOTICE TO R1-DISPENSED WITH)
 -2-  MFA No. 101596 of 2019  THIS MFA FILED U/SEC.173(1) OF MOTOR VEHICLES ACT, 1988, AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 26.09.2018 PASSED IN MVC NO.192/2015 ON THE FILE OF THE SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND JUDICIAL MAGISTRATE FIRST CLASS AND MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS TRIBUNAL, BYADGI,
PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.

THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
Challenging judgment and award dated 26.06.2018 passed by Senior Civil Judge and JMFC and MACT, Byadgi, in MVC No.192/2015, this appeal is filed by claimant for enhancement of compensation.

2. Brief facts as stated are that in an accident that occurred on 07.02.2015, claimant traveling in LGV vehicle bearing registration no.KA-27/B-4060 sustained grievous injuries when it dashed against road side tree due to rash and negligent driving by its driver.
Despite taking treatment, he did not recover fully and sustained permanent physical disability.
3. Alleging loss of earning capacity, he filed claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act against owner and insurer of offending vehicle.
4. Even on service of notice, owner did not appear.
He was placed exparte.
Only respondent no.2-insurer filed objections admitting issuance of insurance policy but, alleging violation.

It was also contended that claimant was gratuitous passenger as it was a goods vehicle and denied age,
occupation, income as well as disability sustained.
5. Based on pleadings, Tribunal framed issues and recorded evidence of claimant as PW1 and Dr.Umanath R. Ullal as PW2 and marked Exhibits P1 to P19.
In rebuttal, official of insurer was examined as RW1 and Exhibits R1 to R3 were marked.

6. On consideration, Tribunal held that accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of insured vehicle by its driver, claimant sustained injuries and permanent physical disability as a Sri.Modinsab S/O Mohammedkasim ... vs Sri.Khadri

on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84124207/
2 result and claimant was entitled for compensation from insurer.
It assessed total compensation of Rs.3,52,836/- with 7% interest and held insurer is liable to pay same.
7. Not satisfied with compensation claimant is in appeal.

Sri. C.M.Hosmani, learned counsel appearing for claimant-appellant submitted that, though claimant had stated that he was working as a vegetable vendor and earning Rs.25,000/- per month, it erred in taking his monthly income as Rs.7,000/- and sought enhancement.
It was further submitted that claimant sustained fracture of right radius and ulna assessed by PW2- Dr.Umanath R.Ullal to cause 45% limb disability.

However,
Tribunal considered meager amount of loss of earning capacity at 15% and sought enhancement.
It was submitted that compensation awarded towards loss of income during laid up period was inadequate.
It was also contended that PW2-Dr.U.R.Ullal deposed that there were implants at fracture site.
However, no compensation was awarded for their removal and sought enhancement of compensation.
Hence, sought to allow appeal.
8. On other hand, Shri S.S.Joshi, learned counsel for respondent-insurer supported award and opposed enhancement.
It was further submitted that claimant sustained fracture of right radius and ulna.

Tribunal awarded total compensation of Rs.3,52,836/- which on over all consideration was adequate and no enhancement was called for.
9.

From above submission, occurrence of accident due to rash and negligent driving of insured vehicle by its driver, claimant sustaining injuries and physical disability therein and liability of insurer to pay compensation to claimant are not in dispute.
There is no appeal by insurer.
Only claimant is seeking enhancement.

Hence point that arises for consideration is:
"Whether claimant is entitled for enhancement of compensation as sought for?"
10.
Claim for enhancement is on limited ground namely monthly income.
Insofar as monthly income, though claimant stated that he was earning Rs.25,000/- per month, same was not substantiated with evidence.

In absence of specific evidence, tribunal would be justified in assessing it notionally, which for year 2015 is Rs.8,000/- as per norms adopted by Karnataka State Legal Services Committee for settlement of cases before Lok Adalath.
Therefore, tribunal would not be justified in taking it at Rs.7,000/-.
It would be just and proper to take it at Rs.8,000/-.
In order to establish disability, claimant produced wound certificate at Ex.P5 and disability certificate- Ex.P17.
He also examined Dr.Umanath R.Ullal as PW2.
From said evidence, it is clear that claimant sustained fracture of right radius and ulna assessed by PW2-Dr.Umanath R.Ullal to cause limb disability to extent of 45%.
However, as claimant is stated to be doing vegetable business, extent of disability sustained might not be substantial.
Tribunal assessed disability at 15%, which is adequate.

Therefore, future loss of income by applying multiplier would be '15' as follows:
"Rs.8,000/- x 15% x 12 x 15 = Rs.2,16,000/-."
11.
Further, fractures normally take three months to heal.

Since monthly income is re- assessed at Rs.8,000/-, compensation towards loss of income during laid up period would be Rs.8,000/- X 3 =
Rs.24,000/-.

3 12.
Tribunal noted that there were implants in situ.
However, no compensation is awarded for future medical expenses for removal.
Therefore, a sum of Rs.25,000/- is awarded towards same.
Tribunal awarded compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards pain and suffering.
Considering fractures, it would be just and proper to award Rs.40,000/- towards same.
Considering nature of fracture and disability sustained, award of Rs.20,000/- towards loss of amenities would not be appropriate.
It is enhanced to Rs.30,000/-.
Tribunal awarded Rs.99,836/- towards medical expenses against bills produced which is in complete reimbursement of amount spent.
Hence, no enhancement is called for.
It is not in dispute that claimant took inpatient treatment for period of 7 days.
Considering nature of fracture and treatment taken, award Rs.10,000/- towards food, nourishment and other incidental expenses would not be justified.
It is enhanced to Rs.20,000/-.

13. Thus, claimant is entitled for re-assessed compensation as follows:-
Sl.no. Heads Amount  (in Rs.)
1. Pain and suffering 40,000/-
2. Loss of amenities and 30,000/-
 future unhappiness 3. Future loss of income 2,16,000/-
4. Medical expenses 99,836/-
5. Loss of income during laid 24,000/-
 up period 6.

Incidental expenses 20,000/-
7.
Future medical expenses 25,000/-

Total: Rs.4,54,836/-
Therefore, point for consideration is answered partly in affirmative as above.

14. Hence following:
- 10 -  ORDER Sri.Modinsab S/O Mohammedkasim ... vs Sri.Khadri on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84124207/

4  i. Appeal is allowed in part.
 ii. Judgment and award dated 26.09.2018,
passed by Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Byadgi, in MVC No.192/2014 is modified.
iii.

Claimant is held entitled for reassessed compensation of Rs.4,54,836/- as against Rs.3,52,836/- awarded by tribunal, which shall carry interest at 6% per annum from date of claim petition till deposit.
iv. Insurer is directed to deposit enhanced compensation within a period of six weeks from date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
v. Directions issued by tribunal regarding  deposit and release would apply  proportionately to enhanced  compensation also.
